Title: Challenging the notion of innate phonetic boundaries.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: 46 infants and 75 3-year-olds
Stimulus_Type: natural and synthetic speech; phonetic contrasts
Outcome: discrimination of phonetic contrasts
Evidence_Quote: In this study, discrimination abilities of 46 infants and 75 3-year-olds were measured for several phonetic contrasts occurring in their native language, using natural and synthetic speech.

Title: DPOAE suppression tuning: cochlear immaturity in premature neonates or auditory aging in normal-hearing adults?
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: normal-hearing school-aged children and adults; premature neonate STCs from a previous study used for comparison
Outcome: children's STCs comparable to adults and different from neonates at 1500 and 6000 Hz; suppression growth not adultlike in children at 6000 Hz only
Evidence_Quote: DPOAE STCs were recorded at 1500, 3000, and 6000 Hz using optimal parameters in normal-hearing children and adults.

Title: Distortion product otoacoustic emission (2f1-f2) amplitude growth in human adults and neonates.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: normal-hearing adults and term-born neonates; premature neonates
Outcome: distortion product otoacoustic emission (2f1-f2) amplitude growth; DPOAE growth functions
Evidence_Quote: The 2f1-f2 DPOAE growth functions were recorded for both age groups at three f2 frequencies.

Title: Moderate noise trauma in juvenile cats results in profound cortical topographic map changes in adulthood.
Target_Age: 5-week-old kittens
Outcome: mild to moderate high-frequency hearing loss and profound reorganization of the auditory cortex frequency map in adulthood
Evidence_Quote: exposure of 5-week-old kittens to a loud 6 kHz tone, producing mild to moderate high-frequency hearing loss

Title: Neurophysiological brainstem investigations in isolated Pierre Robin sequence.
Target_Age: 25 newborn babies with isolated Pierre Robin sequence
Outcome: obstructive apneas; sleep stages; brainstem auditory evoked responses (BAERs); sucking-swallowing disorders
Evidence_Quote: Polysomnography, electromyography (EMG) of the face, tongue, and soft palate, blink reflexes (BRs), EMG during bottle-feeding, and brainstem auditory evoked responses (BAERs) were performed in 25 newborn babies with isolated Pierre Robin sequence (PRS) to aid in evaluation and management.

Title: The effects of maturation and stimulus parameters on the optimal f(2)/f(1) ratio of the 2f(1)-f(2) distortion product otoacoustic emission in neonates(1).
Target_Age: 105 neonates between 30-42 weeks conceptional age and 40 adults
Outcome: no neonate-adult difference in optimum f2/f1 ratio; optimum ratio depends on f2 frequency and primary tone level
Evidence_Quote: The adult group was used to investigate the effect of stimulus level on the optimum f(2)/f(1) ratio for f(2) frequencies from 1.7 to 10 kHz.

Title: Bone conduction experiments in humans - a fluid pathway from bone to ear.
Target_Age: neonates
Stimulus_Type: bone conduction stimulation; bone vibrator stimulation
Outcome: auditory nerve brainstem evoked responses; audiometric responses; audiometric thresholds
Evidence_Quote: Auditory nerve brainstem evoked responses could be recorded in neonates to bone conduction stimulation over the fontanelle and audiometric responses were obtained in neurosurgical patients with the bone vibrator on the skin over a craniotomy.

Title: Maturation of human fetal responses to airborne sound in low- and high-risk fetuses.
Target_Age: low-risk fetuses at 27, 30, 33, and 36 weeks GA (Study 1); high-risk fetuses at 27, 30, 33 weeks GA (Study 2)
Outcome: cardiac acceleration and body movement responses begin at 30 weeks GA; cardiac response threshold decreases from 105-110 dB at 33 weeks to 100-105 dB at 36 weeks
Evidence_Quote: received three sound trials at 90, 100, 105 and 110 dB and three no-stimulus control trials

Title: The effect of parent training in music and multimodal stimulation on parent-neonate interactions in the neonatal intensive care unit.
Target_Age: premature and low birthweight (LBW) infants
Outcome: parent-neonate interactions; weight gain; length of hospitalization; infant stress and nonstress behaviors
Evidence_Quote: This study examined the effects of parent training in music and multimodal stimulation on the quantity and quality of parent-neonate interactions and the weight gain and length of hospitalization of premature and low birthweight (LBW) infants in a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU).

Title: Segmental and syllabic representations in the perception of speech by young infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: 3- to 4-month-old infants
Outcome: categorical representations to syllable-initial consonants; categorical representation of initial and final syllables
Evidence_Quote: the ability of 3- to 4-month-old infants to form categorical representations to syllable-initial consonants in monosyllabic stimuli (experiments 1 and 2) and to initial and final syllables in bisyllabic stimuli (experiments 3 and 4, respectively) was investigated.

Title: Maturation of medial efferent system function in humans.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: human adults, term and premature neonates
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE primary tones with contralateral broadband noise
Outcome: contralateral suppression absent at 6000 Hz but present at 1500 and 3000 Hz; premature neonates show suppression or enhancement (immature medial efferent function)
Evidence_Quote: term and premature neonates at three f2 frequencies: 1500, 3000, and 6000 Hz, using fixed primary tone frequency ratio (f2/f1 = 1.2) and level separation (10 dB, L1 > L2)

Title: Forward masking among infant and adult listeners.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: 3- and 6-month-old infants and adults
Stimulus_Type: tone-burst probe with broadband noise forward masker
Outcome: infants show more forward masking than adults, especially at short masker-probe intervals; susceptibility nearly mature by 6 months
Evidence_Quote: Listeners detected a repeated 1000-Hz probe, with 16-ms rise time, no steady-state duration, and 16-ms fall time. Unmasked thresholds were determined for one group of listeners who were trained to respond when they heard the probe but not at other times. In the masking conditions, each tone burst was preceded by a 100-ms broadband noise masker at 65 dB SPL.

Title: Development of human cochlear active mechanism asymmetry: involvement of the medial olivocochlear system?
Target_Age: pre-term and full-term neonates (73 ears of 38 pre-term and 11 full-term neonates)
Stimulus_Type: contralateral broad band white noise (TEOAE suppression)
Outcome: contralateral suppression of TEOAEs increases with conceptional age; right-ear advantage emerges after 36 weeks
Evidence_Quote: The continuous contralateral stimulation was a broad band white noise, presented at 70 dB SPL.

Title: Presentation of Aural Stimuli to Newborns and Premature Infants: An Audiological Perspective.
Target_Age: premature or term newborns
Outcome: N/A
Evidence_Quote: Articles considered appropriate for inclusion in the analysis met the following criteria: (a) presented data for the effects of music on a dependent measure, (b) had subjects who were identified as either premature or term newborns receiving treatment after birth and prior to discharge from the hospital, and (c) used music for some or all of the aural stimuli.

Title: Modeling otoacoustic emissions by active nonlinear oscillators.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: no participants (modeling study compared with experimental data of neonatal spontaneous and evoked OAEs)
Stimulus_Type: none (theoretical oscillator models of otoacoustic emissions)
Outcome: exponential decay with damping coefficients in the 20-200 Hz range fits OAE data; not compatible with a Van der Pol oscillator
Evidence_Quote: an approximately exponential decay law, with characteristic damping coefficients in the 20-200 Hz range, was found to fit the data

Title: Basic properties of the sound-evoked post-auricular muscle response (PAMR).
Target_Age: human subjects including very young infants (response reaches adult values by 12 months)
Stimulus_Type: click and tone-burst stimuli (post-auricular muscle response)
Outcome: PAMR obtainable within 20 dB of subjective detection threshold; response spectrum mostly between 25 and 200 Hz
Evidence_Quote: can be evoked with tone-bursts between 500 Hz and 16 kHz

Title: A correlation method for detecting the sound-evoked post-auricular muscle response (PAMR).
Target_Age: four adults and two infants
Outcome: sound-evoked post-auricular muscle response (PAMR)
Evidence_Quote: We have made detailed measurements of the sound-evoked post-auricular muscle response (PAMR) in four adults and two infants, in an attempt to understand the inter-relationships between sound level, potentiation of the PAMR with voluntary PAM contraction or eye rotation, electromyographic (EMG) noise, amplitude of the PAMR, and a correlation measure of the presence of the PAMR.

Title: The impact of early onset otitis media on babbling and early language development.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: birth through 6 months of age; 6 through 18 months of age
Outcome: canonical babble; canonical syllable production; expressive vocabulary size
Evidence_Quote: The purpose of this study was to investigate the impact of OM on the development of canonical babble in children who experienced at least one episode during the period birth through 6 months of age, in comparison with children who did not experience OM during this period.

Title: Chaotic and periodic heart rate dynamics in uncomplicated intrauterine growth restricted fetuses.
Target_Age: normal fetuses (n = 192) and uncomplicated intrauterine growth restricted fetuses (n = 86), 31-42 weeks of gestation
Outcome: IUGR fetuses show lower heart-rate complexity and higher low-frequency (0.04-0.15 Hz) periodicity than normal fetuses
Evidence_Quote: The low-frequency (0.04-0.15 Hz) component and, therefore, the periodicity of the low-frequency range was significantly higher than that of the normal fetuses during all the gestational weeks.

Title: Distortion product otoacoustic emissions in human newborns and adults. I. Frequency effects.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: human newborns (term and preterm) and adults
Outcome: newborns have larger 2 f1-f2 DPOAE amplitudes than adults at lower f2; similar amplitudes at the highest f2 assessed
Evidence_Quote: At the highest frequencies assessed (f2 = 4.2-9.9 kHz) all subjects had similar amplitude 2 f1-f2 DPOAEs. At lower frequencies adult 2 f1-f2 amplitudes were significantly less than those of newborns. At the lowest frequencies reliably assessed (f2 = 1.5-2.1 kHz) term newborns had significantly larger 2 f1-f2 DPOAEs than preterm newborns.

Title: Distortion product otoacoustic emissions in human newborns and adults. II. Level effects.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: human newborns and adults
Outcome: distortion product otoacoustic emissions (DPOAEs)
Evidence_Quote: This study varied the levels of the primaries and recorded distortion product otoacoustic emissions (DPOAEs) from human newborns and adults.
